constraint_review: Mass 60 kg limit is met with 46 kg summed standing mass versus 60 kg leaving 14 kg margin. Stowed box 1.0 by 0.5 by 0.5 m is met on the board at 0.90 by 0.42 by 0.45 m stowed with widening after start, though the width stack needs a summed check in detail. Digging BP-1 simulant is met in calculation with 11 N kerf draft well below 294 N traction and 112 s fill to 15 kg. Blind remote operation is met in concept with drive/dig/mast cameras plus heartbeat stop and fiducial reset for out-of-sight control.
feedback:
Overall this narrow-kerf plus bucket-ladder with screw-metered tilt pour is a physically coherent blind digger and I would release it to detail design. The cutting load of order 10 N against traction of order 300 N, lifting energy under 1 Wh against a 480 Wh pack, 46 kg against 60 kg, and stowed size inside the box all close with large margin, and the architecture is a credible lightweight, stowable derivative of the CHONDROBOT-2 bucket-ladder prototype at 65 kg and 1.21 by 0.66 m. My main worry is flow stoppage of cohesive BP-1 over the 150 mm outlet plus dust on the bin fiducial, followed by width stack-up and worst-case coasting before the heartbeat stops the machine.

I rechecked the deciding relations. Cutting is modeled as width times cohesion term plus weight term, F equals w times c times d plus one-half rho g d squared times N, which matches the code behind the 32.9 N full-width estimate for 0.3 m width, 500 Pa cohesion, 50 mm depth, 1500 kg per cubic metre and factor 4.6 (E9). Arithmetic gives 0.3 times 25 plus 84.6 equals 32.9 N, and linear scaling to 0.1 m kerf gives 11 N (E64), correct for a cohesion-dominated shallow cut. Traction is modeled as mu times weight, W equals m times g. Earth weight for 60 kg is 589 N (E22), and 294 N traction (E23) implies mu near 0.5 for grouser wheels, plausible on loose soil and supported by the Moonraker grouser work read from the opened page (E14). Even at the 46 kg design mass traction is about 226 N, still more than 20 times the 11 N kerf draft, so the work principle holds. Ground pressure is modeled as weight over contact area, p equals W divided by n times b times l with l near sqrt of D times sinkage. With four 0.15 m wide wheels and 0.063 m contact length from 0.2 m diameter and 0.02 m sinkage the board gets 15.6 kPa (E25), arithmetic correct and ordinary beside a standing person at tens of kPa. Dig power is modeled as force times chain speed, P equals F times v. The board multiplies 32.9 N by 0.5 m per s to get 16.4 W (E59), arithmetic correct, but that uses full-width force while the design digs at 11 N, so true cutting power is near 5.5 W plus under 1 W to lift 0.13 kg per s through 0.5 m; the error is conservative for battery sizing. Dig energy E equals P times t gives 16.45 W times 112 s divided by 3600 equals 0.51 Wh (E60), arithmetic correct and tiny beside the 24 V 20 Ah pack at 480 Wh, and the mixed-duty use near 100 Wh (E44) leaves factor four. Frame sag is modeled as cantilever deflection delta equals P times L cubed divided by 3 times E times I. Second moment for two 25.4 mm outside 3 mm wall tubes as B fourth minus b fourth over 12 times two gives 4.58e-08 m fourth (E61), correct, and 300 N on 0.5 m with 68.9 GPa gives 3.96 mm (E63), arithmetic correct and acceptable, though 300 N is a little light versus half the 46 kg machine plus 15 kg soil at about 373 N which would give near 4.9 mm, still small. Braking is modeled as coast plus brake, d equals v times T plus v squared over 2a. At 0.5 m per s with 2 m per s squared decel the brake-only distance is 0.0625 m (E23) and with 0.5 s timeout total is near 0.31 m (E32), arithmetic correct and ordinary beside a step. Dump clearance as pivot height minus lip height, 0.55 m minus 0.40 m equals 0.15 m (E51), arithmetic correct as a static number, tilt kinematics still to show in detail. Drift bounded to 0.10 to 0.15 m with 5 m fiducial resets (E33) and final visual error near 0.03 to 0.04 m at 1 to 2 m range (E58) are plausible orders for odometry plus tag aiding. Outlet area pi times d squared over 4 for 0.15 m gives 0.0177 m squared (E69), arithmetic correct.

The design agrees with itself except for drawing and labeling gaps that do not break the load, material or signal paths. Chassis at 900 to 1050 mm with stowed 0.90 m and deployed 1.05 m by 0.68 m track (E51) beside folded side and top views (E24) and dump and track views (E53) is coherent if the 600 to 800 mm ladder and kerf fold inside the 0.90 m. Width is the tight point for detail: stowed 0.42 m track plus 0.12 m wheels and 0.025 m spin gap can exceed 0.5 m if track is center to center, so detail should sum chassis plus folded arms plus wheel widths plus spin gap across, ladder overhang front to back, and stacked heights against 1.0 by 0.5 by 0.5 m, and show the folded ladder and kerf inside 0.90 m in side and top pose. As drawn the board value 0.90 by 0.42 by 0.45 m passes, so this is advice not a block. Loads label cutting resistance as down where draft is mainly horizontal, but support under wheels up with soil weight down still gives a closed vertical path, and the fused 24 V bus from packs to drives, dig, lift and compute with video and heartbeat to the sealed operator (E32) gives closed energy and signal paths from trench views to commands. Functions all have means: wheels for traverse, kerf chain for loosen, ladder for collect and elevate, wedge hopper for contain, screw plus rear tilt for discharge, cameras plus computer plus fiducial for blind coordination, so no missing function, and the chief made explicit deferrals.

For worst case the board often shows nominal. Pressure used 60 kg while the machine plus one trip is 46 plus 15 equals 61 kg, essentially the same 16 kPa, acceptable. Traction used 60 kg while the light empty machine gives less, still factor 20 on kerf draft, acceptable. Stopping shows 0.308 m for 0.5 s timeout but also 0.56 m for 1.0 s and 1.06 m for 2.0 s in the same run (E32), so detail should carry the longest credible latency and show the pour can still stay over a 0.4 m bin mouth from 1 to 2 m (E58). Stability quotes 206 Nm over 44 Nm factor 4.67 (E23) in one place and factor 1.69 level in another, so detail should recompute tip moment with 15 kg raised in rear tilt on level ground as the worst holding case. Hopper walls at 60 deg for 39 to 51 deg friction soil (E3) with steep smooth-wall practice (E7)(E8) is directionally right, but arching over 150 mm with half-full 15 kg trips in a 20 L 30 kg-max hopper at 1500 kg per cubic metre (E10)(E11) with 112 s ladder versus 450 s scraper fill (E11) remains the open physics, correctly carried as detail-test planning with screw torque to break a bridge, edge wear, and tag visibility in dust. None of these needs a bench to accept the concept; they belong in detail analysis using calculation and simulation with opened sources.

On the four review checks: no function lacks a means. Mass sums to 46 kg in two consistent sums (E62)(E68) against an earlier 47 kg sum (E41) with the same parts, a harmless 1 kg deviation, and 14 kg margin remains (E67); size is computed against its numbers on the board and the directional sum above is detail confirmation. Numbered limits are otherwise computed against their numbers. Two values appear for the same quantity in several places, full-width 32.9 N versus kerf 11 N, 16.4 W versus 5.5 W implied, 72.9 mm and 36.5 mm early sag versus 3.96 mm stiffened, 0.062 m versus 0.308 m versus 1.06 m stop, 4.67 versus 1.69 tip factor; I used the design values 11 N, 46 kg, 3.96 mm, 0.308 m nominal and flagged the conservative or worst-case partner. Material flow from kerf slot through side spoil rows into the wide ladder through the gravity chute into the hopper through the screw over the lip (E65)(E13) is bridged on paper but the kerf-to-ladder handoff geometry must be fixed in the folded and working poses in detail. Signal from forward, dig and mast cameras through encoder and telemetry with heartbeat stop and current-limit backout in 0.6 s (E58) to fiducial creep align in 1.5 s is closed. There is no open blocking objection after two cycles and all leads marked ready, so the meeting facts leave the concept settled.

Literature weakness matters where it decides flow: BP-1 density, cohesion and friction (E3)(E4), cutting models (E5)(E6), Jenike walls (E7)(E8), tip rules (E47)(E48) and tag accuracy (E54)(E55) rest on search results never opened, weaker than the opened grouser rover source (E14), the opened teleoperation and e-stop sources (E26)(E27), and the opened odometry discussion (E28). Detail should replace those with opened-page values for a Jenike critical-outlet check. Build is ordinary shop work, TIG-welded 6061-T6 twin tube, bolted arms and steel grouser wheels, chain and ladder, steel wedge hopper with screw, LiFePO4 bus and cameras, cost class 1k to 10k, no exotic process. Compared with CHONDROBOT-2 at 8 kg per min and full cycle in 5 min with 18 kg collector to a 0.5 m bin, this concept trades full-width digging for 100 mm kerf pre-cut feeding wide pickup, trades plain dump for metered tilt plus auger, and trades fixed footprint for folding arms to meet 60 kg and the start box, a genuine adaptation rather than a copy.
